posts.name: Harish Chauhan
posts.cooked: hey, I have opted for system command this sem…. this is the first time i am getting confused from where should i start…. there was a video vm login process…. i didnt get what was that…. can anyone please explain from where should i start(eg. should i start with week one content and download and launch linux acc. to that) i am just getting confused about how to setup linux and that the vn part can anyone please tell.

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked:
1. To practice the commands taught in the lectures, you’ll need a Linux environment. As discussed in the first lecture, you have a few options. You can either launch a virtual machine using software like VMware, or you can download and use the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). Your other option is to dual boot Linux with Windows.

    I will suggest you start with WSL, as it is the easiest to get started with.

  2. The VM login video explains how to access the virtual machine provided by the course team. You will use this VM to solve your Bi-weekly Programming Tests (BPTs).

    Your scores from these tests are important, as they determine your eligibility for the OPPE and also carry some weightage in the final grading formula.

For now, you can get started with setting up WSL.

posts.name: Harish Chauhan
posts.cooked: ok thanks…. and one more thing can i do in window powershell?

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked: Yes. Once you connect to the course VM through SSH, you connect to a linux enviornment. Then you can use linux commands there.

posts.name: ASHUTOSH kumar
posts.cooked:
i have downloaded oracle vm created vm but problem i am facing they are too slow for my pc any good free alternative please share.

Thank you

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked: Yes. Virtual Machines are quite heavy. You can download WSL for starting and if you want a GUI linux experience then you can dual boot as well.

posts.name: Jagruti
posts.cooked:
[quote=“Mrinal.exe, post:2, topic:187568”]

The VM login video explains how to access the virtual machine provided by the course team. You will use this VM to solve your Bi-weekly Programming Tests (BPTs).

[/quote]

Can bpts be done using wsl ?

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked: NO! You cannot do BPTs on wsl locally. But you can connect to course VM from WSL and complete the BPTs there.

posts.name: Shiva Prakash
posts.cooked: Do I need to install WSL if I have a Mac?

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked: No, if you Mac you can practice the commands on your system. WSL not required. @ShivaP06
